A partition [MATH: P] of a closed interval [MATH: [a,b]] is a finite sequence of real numbers taken from [MATH: [a,b]] such that

[MATH: a = x_0 < x_1< x_2 < \ldots < x_n = b\,.]

We can express [MATH: P] using set notation as [MATH: P=\{x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_n\}.]

With that in mind, let's consider each statement:

  • Statement I is not a partition of [MATH: [1,9]] since it does not include the right endpoint [MATH: b=9.]

  • Statement II is a partition of [MATH: [1,9].]

  • Statement III is a partition of [MATH: [1,9].]

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."

items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose we have the partition [MATH: P=\{0,2,5,6\}] of the interval [MATH: [a,b]=[0,6].] Then, we have
[MATH: a=\underbrace{0}_{\large x_0} < \underbrace{2}_{\large x_1} < \underbrace{5}_{\large x_2} < \underbrace{6}_{\large x_3} =b.]

Content:
This partition breaks up the interval [MATH: [0,6]] into the union of the following subintervals:

Content:
[MATH: [0,2] \cup [2,5] \cup [5,6]]

Content:
The length of the [MATH: i]th subinterval, denoted [MATH: \Delta x_i,] is simply the difference of the endpoints:

Content:
- The length of the first interval [MATH: [0,2],] denoted [MATH: \Delta x_1,] is
[MATH: Δx_{1}|= x_{1} − x_{0}; = 2 − 0; = 2.]
- The length of the second interval [MATH: [2,5],] denoted [MATH: \Delta x_2,] is
[MATH: Δx_{2}|= x_{2} − x_{1}; = 5 − 2; = 3.]
- The length of the third interval [MATH: [5,6],] denoted [MATH: \Delta x_3,] is
[MATH: Δx_{3}|= x_{3} − x_{2}; = 6 − 5; = 1.]

Content:
Therefore,
[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(3)Δx_{i}|= Δx_{1} + Δx_{2} + Δx_{3}; = 2 + 3 + 1; = 6,]
which is just the length of the interval [MATH: [0, 6].]

Content:
Note: In general, for any partition [MATH: P=\{x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_m\}] of an interval [MATH: [a,b],] the sum [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^m\Delta x_i] is just the length of the interval [MATH: [a, b],] because

Content:
[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(m)Δx_{i}|= Δx_{1} + Δx_{2} + Δx_{3} + ⋯ + Δx_{m}; = (x_{1} − x_{0}) + (x_{2} − x_{1}) + (x_{3} − x_{2}) + ⋯ + (x_{m} − x_{m − 1}); = (x_{1} − x_{0}) + (x_{2} − x_{1}) + (x_{3} − x_{2}) + ⋯ + (x_{m} − x_{m − 1}); = − x_{0} + x_{m}; = x_{m} − x_{0}; = b − a.]

sections.normalized_html:
First, we take the factor [MATH: 3] outside the summation:

[MATH: ∑_(j = 1)^(n)3Δy_{j} = 3∑_(j = 1)^(n)Δy_{j}]

Note that [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{j=1}^n \Delta y_j] is just the length of the interval [MATH: [-3, 5],] because

[MATH: ∑_(j = 1)^(n)Δy_{j}|= Δy_{1} + Δy_{2} + Δy_{3} + ⋯ + Δy_{n}; = (y_{1} − y_{0}) + (y_{2} − y_{1}) + (y_{3} − y_{2}) + ⋯ + (y_{n} − y_{n − 1}); = (y_{1} − y_{0}) + (y_{2} − y_{1}) + (y_{3} − y_{2}) + ⋯ + (y_{n} − y_{n − 1}); = − y_{0} + y_{n}; = y_{n} − y_{0}; = 5 − (− 3); = 5 + 3; = 8.]

Therefore,

[MATH: {3}\sum_{j=1}^n \Delta y_j = 3 \cdot 8 = 24.]

Explanation:
We can simplify the given summation as follows:

[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(m)(x_{i} + x_{i − 1})Δx_{i}|= (x_{1} + x_{0})Δx_{1} + (x_{2} + x_{1})Δx_{2} + ⋯ + (x_{m} + x_{m − 1})Δx_{m}; = (x_{1} + x_{0})(x_{1} − x_{0}) + (x_{2} + x_{1})(x_{2} − x_{1}) + ⋯ + (x_{m} + x_{m − 1})(x_{m} − x_{m − 1}); = (x_{1}^{2} − x_{0}^{2}) + (x_{2}^{2} − x_{1}^{2}) + ⋯ + (x_{m}^{2} − x_{m − 1}^{2}); = (x_{1}^{2} − x_{0}^{2}) + (x_{2}^{2} − x_{1}^{2}) + ⋯ + (x_{m}^{2} − x_{m − 1}^{2}); = − x_{0}^{2} + x_{m}^{2}; = x_{m}^{2} − x_{0}^{2}]

Now, since [MATH: x_0 = -3] and [MATH: x_m = 4] are the endpoints of our partition, we have

[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(m)(x_{i} + x_{i − 1})Δx_{i}|= x_{m}^{2} − x_{0}^{2}; = 4^{2} − (− 3)^{2}; = 7.]

Item 5 — Tutorial: Sums Over Partitions

Content:
Suppose we have the partition [MATH: P=\{0,2,5,6\}] of the interval [MATH: [a,b]=[0,6].] Then, we have
[MATH: a=\underbrace{0}_{\large x_0} < \underbrace{2}_{\large x_1} < \underbrace{5}_{\large x_2} < \underbrace{6}_{\large x_3} =b.]

Content:
This partition breaks up the interval [MATH: [0,6]] into the union of the following subintervals:

Content:
[MATH: [0,2] \cup [2,5] \cup [5,6]]

Content:
The length of the [MATH: i]th subinterval, denoted [MATH: \Delta x_i,] is simply the difference of the endpoints:

Content:
- The length of the first interval [MATH: [0,2],] denoted [MATH: \Delta x_1,] is
[MATH: Δx_{1}|= x_{1} − x_{0}; = 2 − 0; = 2.]
- The length of the second interval [MATH: [2,5],] denoted [MATH: \Delta x_2,] is
[MATH: Δx_{2}|= x_{2} − x_{1}; = 5 − 2; = 3.]
- The length of the third interval [MATH: [5,6],] denoted [MATH: \Delta x_3,] is
[MATH: Δx_{3}|= x_{3} − x_{2}; = 6 − 5; = 1.]

Content:
Therefore,
[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(3)Δx_{i}|= Δx_{1} + Δx_{2} + Δx_{3}; = 2 + 3 + 1; = 6,]
which is just the length of the interval [MATH: [0, 6].]

Content:
Note: In general, for any partition [MATH: P=\{x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_m\}] of an interval [MATH: [a,b],] the sum [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^m\Delta x_i] is just the length of the interval [MATH: [a, b],] because

Content:
[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(m)Δx_{i}|= Δx_{1} + Δx_{2} + Δx_{3} + ⋯ + Δx_{m}; = (x_{1} − x_{0}) + (x_{2} − x_{1}) + (x_{3} − x_{2}) + ⋯ + (x_{m} − x_{m − 1}); = (x_{1} − x_{0}) + (x_{2} − x_{1}) + (x_{3} − x_{2}) + ⋯ + (x_{m} − x_{m − 1}); = − x_{0} + x_{m}; = x_{m} − x_{0}; = b − a.]

Item 6 — Example: Computing Simple Sums Over Partitions of the Real Line

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we take the factor [MATH: 3] outside the summation:

[MATH: ∑_(j = 1)^(n)3Δy_{j} = 3∑_(j = 1)^(n)Δy_{j}]

Note that [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{j=1}^n \Delta y_j] is just the length of the interval [MATH: [-3, 5],] because

[MATH: ∑_(j = 1)^(n)Δy_{j}|= Δy_{1} + Δy_{2} + Δy_{3} + ⋯ + Δy_{n}; = (y_{1} − y_{0}) + (y_{2} − y_{1}) + (y_{3} − y_{2}) + ⋯ + (y_{n} − y_{n − 1}); = (y_{1} − y_{0}) + (y_{2} − y_{1}) + (y_{3} − y_{2}) + ⋯ + (y_{n} − y_{n − 1}); = − y_{0} + y_{n}; = y_{n} − y_{0}; = 5 − (− 3); = 5 + 3; = 8.]

Therefore,

[MATH: {3}\sum_{j=1}^n \Delta y_j = 3 \cdot 8 = 24.]

Example Prompt:
Let [MATH: P = \left\{x_0, x_1, \ldots, x_m\right\}] be a partition of the interval [MATH: [-3, 4].] If [MATH: \Delta x_i = x_i - x_{i-1},] calculate [MATH: \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^m (x_i + x_{i-1})\Delta x_i .]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We can simplify the given summation as follows:

[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(m)(x_{i} + x_{i − 1})Δx_{i}|= (x_{1} + x_{0})Δx_{1} + (x_{2} + x_{1})Δx_{2} + ⋯ + (x_{m} + x_{m − 1})Δx_{m}; = (x_{1} + x_{0})(x_{1} − x_{0}) + (x_{2} + x_{1})(x_{2} − x_{1}) + ⋯ + (x_{m} + x_{m − 1})(x_{m} − x_{m − 1}); = (x_{1}^{2} − x_{0}^{2}) + (x_{2}^{2} − x_{1}^{2}) + ⋯ + (x_{m}^{2} − x_{m − 1}^{2}); = (x_{1}^{2} − x_{0}^{2}) + (x_{2}^{2} − x_{1}^{2}) + ⋯ + (x_{m}^{2} − x_{m − 1}^{2}); = − x_{0}^{2} + x_{m}^{2}; = x_{m}^{2} − x_{0}^{2}]

Now, since [MATH: x_0 = -3] and [MATH: x_m = 4] are the endpoints of our partition, we have

[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(m)(x_{i} + x_{i − 1})Δx_{i}|= x_{m}^{2} − x_{0}^{2}; = 4^{2} − (− 3)^{2}; = 7.]
